verdict.rationale: Maritime documents that a Dockerfile-based container can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL. That gives a public endpoint for a service running inside a Maritime-managed container. However, it is a web-app deployment feature, not documented port exposure or preview URLs for an agent's sandbox or VM. missing for 10: exposing arbitrary ports from an agent sandbox, preview-URL semantics (per-port or ephemeral URLs), access controls on exposed URLs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a port from the sandbox on a public preview URL to reach services running inside

citations.quote: Any repo with a Dockerfile can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL. Maritime builds it, runs it serverlessly, puts it to sleep when idle, and wakes it on the next visit.
Any repo with a Dockerfile can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL.
